(Disease/Condition) a. Rod cells 1. The point of highest visual acuity and resolution b. Cone cells 2. Responsible for twilight (scotopic) vision c. Blind spot 3. An area completely devoid of photoreceptor cells d. Fovea centralis 4. Responsible for daylight (photopic) and colour vision Select the correct answer using the codes given below: a b c d
questions.question_type: Match the Following — Two-List Matching — Answer-Code Matrix
questions.explanation:
Rod cells: The retina contains two major types of photoreceptor cells. Rods contain a purplish-red protein called rhodopsin (visual purple), which contains a derivative of Vitamin A. They are highly sensitive to dim light and are responsible for twilight or night vision (scotopic vision). They do not play a role in colour differentiation.

Cone cells: Cones are responsible for daylight vision (photopic vision) and colour vision. There are three specific types of cone cells in the human eye that respond to red, green, and blue light. The sensation of different colours is produced by various combinations of these cones and their photopigments.

Blind spot: The optic nerve leaves the eye and the retinal blood vessels enter it at a specific point slightly above the posterior pole of the eyeball. Photoreceptor cells (both rods and cones) are completely absent in this specific region. Therefore, no image is formed here, earning it the name “blind spot.”

Fovea centralis: At the posterior pole of the eye, lateral to the blind spot, there is a yellowish pigmented spot called the macula lutea with a central pit called the fovea. The fovea is a thinnedout portion of the retina where only cone cells are densely packed. It is the exact point where visual acuity (resolution of the image) is the greatest.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of Hepatitis viruses and their primary characteristics is incorrectly matched?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: Hepatitis A : Transmitted primarily through the consumption of contaminated food and water.
options.B: Hepatitis B : The only DNA virus in this group, transmitted via infected blood and body fluids.
options.C: Hepatitis C : Preventable through a highly effective, globally administered recombinant vaccine.
options.D: Hepatitis D : A defective virus that strictly requires a pre-existing Hepatitis B infection to replicate.

questions.explanation:
Pair A is correctly matched: Hepatitis A is a highly contagious liver infection caused by the Hepatitis A virus (HAV). Unlike the other strains, it is primarily transmitted via the faecal-oral route, usually through the consumption of contaminated drinking water or unhygienic food. It typically causes an acute, self-limiting illness rather than a chronic disease.

Pair B is correctly matched: Hepatitis B is unique among the common hepatitis viruses because it possesses a double-stranded DNA genome (all others are RNA viruses). It is transmitted through exposure to infectious blood, semen, and other body fluids, including transmission from an infected mother to her infant at birth.

Pair C is incorrectly matched: There is currently no vaccine available to prevent Hepatitis C. It is a blood-borne RNA virus most commonly transmitted through sharing unsterilized needles or unsafe medical practices. However, while there is no vaccine, modern Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) medicines can completely cure over 95% of Hepatitis C infections.

Pair D is correctly matched: Hepatitis D (the Delta virus) is an incomplete, defective RNA virus. It cannot replicate or cause infection inside the human body on its own. It strictly requires the helper function of the Hepatitis B virus (HBV) surface antigen to multiply in liver cells. Therefore, Hepatitis D only occurs as a co-infection or super-infection in individuals who already have Hepatitis B.

Additional Facts:

3 Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP): The Government of India provides the Hepatitis B vaccine free of cost under the UIP. The first dose is crucially administered to infants within 24 hours of birth to prevent vertical (mother-to-child) transmission.

3 Chronic Liver Disease: Hepatitis B and C are the most dangerous strains globally because they frequently lead to chronic (lifelong) infections. If left untreated, they are the leading causes of liver cirrhosis (severe scarring) and hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer).

3 Nobel Prize 2020: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2020 was jointly awarded to Harvey J. Alter, Michael Houghton, and Charles M. Rice for their groundbreaking discovery of the Hepatitis C virus, which led to the development of life-saving antiviral drugs.

questions.q: The cell is regarded as the fundamental structural and functional unit of life because:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: Every cell possesses a membrane-bound nucleus that regulates metabolic activities.
options.B: Anything lacking a complete cellular organisation cannot independently perform all essential life processes.
options.C: All cells contain mitochondria for continuous energy production.
options.D: Cells possess a rigid outer cell wall that protects genetic material from degradation.

questions.explanation:
Statement A is incorrect: While eukaryotes (plants, animals, fungi) have a true membrane-bound nucleus, prokaryotes (bacteria and archaea) are complete, independently living cells that entirely lack a defined nucleus. Their genetic material is naked and lies free in the cytoplasm.

Statement B is correct: Unicellular organisms are capable of independent existence and performing the essential functions of life. Therefore, anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent living. This is exactly why entities like viruses are considered to be on the borderline of living and non-living; they lack a complete cellular structure and their own metabolic machinery, forcing them to rely entirely on a host cell’s machinery to replicate.

30

Statement C is incorrect: While mitochondria are the “powerhouses” of eukaryotic cells, prokaryotic cells do not possess membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria or chloroplasts. Instead, prokaryotes utilise specialised extensions of their plasma membrane (like mesosomes) for cellular respiration and energy production.

Statement D is incorrect: A cell wall is not a universal feature of all cells. While plants, fungi, and most bacteria have a rigid cell wall, animal cells completely lack one, possessing only a flexible, semipermeable plasma membrane.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Fluid Mosaic Model of the cell membrane: 1. The fluid nature of the membrane is due to the flexible bilayer of lipid molecules. 2. The mosaic appearance arises from protein molecules embedded within the lipid bilayer. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Statement 1 is correct: Proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972, the Fluid Mosaic Model is the universally accepted description of the cell membrane. The foundation of the membrane is a phospholipid bilayer (a double layer of fats). This lipid layer is not solid or rigid; rather, it behaves like a viscous fluid, allowing the membrane to be flexible and dynamic.

Statement 2 is correct: The cell membrane is not made exclusively of fats. Scattered throughout this “sea” of fluid lipids are various proteins, resembling a mosaic pattern. These embedded proteins act like gatekeepers, channels, and pumps to help transport vital nutrients, water, and waste products in and out of the cell.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding recent artificial intelligence models in biological and health sciences are correct? 1. AlphaFold, developed by Google DeepMind, predicts the three-dimensional structure of proteins from their amino acid sequences. 2. BioEmu-1, a deep learning model developed by Microsoft, is designed to classify the effects of protein-coding genetic variants to predict human DNA mutations. 3. AlphaGenome was developed collaboratively by Google DeepMind and Yale University to interpret biological interactions by analysing the language of individual cells. How many of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_type: Numerical/Calculation — Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Statement 1 is correct: AlphaFold (developed by Google DeepMind) earned developers Demis Hassabis and John Jumper a Nobel prize for its ability to predict complex protein structures and how they fold from their amino acid sequences.

Statement 2 is incorrect: While BioEmu-1 is developed by Microsoft, its purpose is to predict the full range of shapes a protein naturally explores under biological conditions. The model that predicts the impact of DNA mutations and categorises variants is AlphaGenome (and its complementary model AlphaMissense).

Statement 3 is incorrect: AlphaGenome was introduced by Google DeepMind alone to predict how DNA mutations affect gene regulation.

3 The model designed to understand the language of individual cells and biological interactions is C2S-SCALE, developed by Google DeepMind and Yale University.

questions.q: Which animal group is considered the primary natural reservoir of the monkeypox virus?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Mpox is a viral zoonotic disease caused by the monkeypox virus. Despite its misleading name, nonhuman primates are not the primary natural reservoir. Extensive ecological studies indicate that various species of small African rodents, such as rope squirrels, tree squirrels, and Gambian pouched rats, serve as the main reservoir hosts that sustain the virus in the wild.

Monkeys were simply the first animals in which the disease was discovered during a laboratory outbreak in 1958, which is how the virus got its name. However, they are considered incidental hosts, much like humans, rather than the natural biological reservoir.

Bats are the natural reservoirs for several highly lethal zoonotic viruses, including Nipah, Ebola, and Rabies. They are not associated with the transmission cycle of the monkeypox virus.

Birds are primarily associated with the transmission of pathogens like avian influenza (Bird Flu) and the West Nile virus. They do not harbour or transmit mammalian orthopoxviruses.

Additional Facts:

3 Pathogen Family: The monkeypox virus belongs to the Orthopoxvirus genus within the Poxviridae family. This is the exact same viral family that includes the variola virus, which historically caused Smallpox.

In 2022, the World Health Organisation (WHO) officially recommended using the new synonym “Mpox”. This change was implemented to reduce the global stigma, discrimination, and racism associated with the original name.

The virus is biologically divided into two distinct genetic clades: Clade I (formerly the Congo Basin clade, which is highly virulent and lethal) and Clade II (formerly the West African clade, which causes less severe illness).

Because the viruses are closely related, epidemiological data shows that the traditional Smallpox vaccine provides approximately 85% cross-protective immunity against Mpox.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the architecture and functional principle of a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: A single neural network designed to predict future trends from historical numerical data
options.B: Two neural networks trained in adversarial competition to generate highly realistic synthetic data
options.C: A decentralised peer-to-peer computational network used for the validation of smart contracts
options.D: A quantum computational algorithm developed for cryptographic decryption

questions.explanation:
A GAN consists of two distinct neural networks, the Generator and the Discriminator, locked in a continuous game. The Generator tries to create fake data (like a fake photograph of a human face),

31

while the Discriminator acts as a detective, trying to guess if the image is real or fake. This competition forces the Generator to become incredibly good at creating hyper-realistic synthetic outputs.

Additional facts:

3 Deepfakes: GANs are the primary underlying technology used to create “Deepfakes”, highly realistic but entirely synthetic videos or audio recordings of real people saying or doing things they never did.

3 Zero-Sum Game: The architecture is based on game theory. The Generator only “wins” when it successfully fools the Discriminator.

3 Applications Beyond Media: In biotechnology, GANs are now being used to design entirely new molecular structures for drug discovery by predicting how synthetic proteins will fold and interact.

questions.q: In plant cells, the conversion of solar energy into chemical energy during photosynthesis primarily occurs in:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Chloroplasts are specialised plastids found primarily in the mesophyll cells of plant leaves. They contain the green pigment chlorophyll, which is essential for trapping solar energy (light energy). During the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis, this trapped solar energy is utilised to synthesise energy-rich chemical molecules, specifically ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) and NADPH. This specific process of creating ATP using light energy is known as photophosphorylation.

Mitochondria are the “powerhouses” of the cell and generate the vast majority of cellular ATP, they do so through cellular respiration (oxidative phosphorylation) by breaking down glucose, not by capturing solar energy.

Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures containing rich hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases). They are primarily responsible for intracellular digestion and clearing cellular waste, often referred to as the “suicide bags” of the cell.

Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) is a complex network of tubular membranes. Rough ER (with ribosomes) is involved in protein synthesis and secretion, while Smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis. It does not play a role in converting solar energy to ATP.

questions.q: Which human organ is primarily associated with the most serious malignancies caused by Human Papillomavirus (HPV)?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
The Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted viral infection globally. While many strains cause benign warts, persistent infection with “high-risk” strains (specifically HPV 16 and 18) is the primary biological cause of almost all cases of cervical cancer. The cervix is the lower, narrow end of the uterus that opens into the vagina.

Additional Facts:

3 CERVAVAC: This is India’s first indigenously developed Quadrivalent Human Papillomavirus (qHPV) vaccine. It was developed by the Serum Institute of India (SII) in Pune, making cervical cancer prevention significantly more affordable.

3 Public Health Burden: Cervical cancer is the second most frequent cancer among women in India, despite being one of the most preventable forms of cancer through timely vaccination and regular Pap smear screenings.

3 Target Demographic: The World Health Organisation (WHO) and the Government of India heavily recommend administering the HPV vaccine to pre-adolescent girls, ideally between the ages of 9 and 14 years, before any potential exposure to the virus.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the mechanism of peripheral immune tolerance?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: It inactivates or suppresses self-reactive lymphocytes that have escaped into the secondary lymphoid tissues
options.B: It destroys self-reactive immature T-cells during their initial development strictly within the thymus gland
options.C: It utilises circulating macrophages to indiscriminately engulf and destroy foreign bacterial pathogens entering the bloodstream
options.D: It actively stimulates memory B-cells to produce large quantities of autoantibodies against healthy tissues

questions.explanation:
Option A is correct: Peripheral immune tolerance is a crucial secondary safeguard mechanism of the human immune system. It takes place outside the primary lymphoid organs, specifically in the peripheral tissues and lymph nodes. Its primary function is to neutralise mature, self-reactive T-cells and B-cells that mistakenly escaped initial screening. It achieves this by forcing these rogue cells into a state of permanent unresponsiveness (anergy), triggering their self-destruction (apoptosis), or suppressing them using specialised Regulatory T-cells (Tregs).

Option B is incorrect: This describes Central Immune Tolerance. Central tolerance is the primary screening process that occurs during the initial maturation of lymphocytes directly within the thymus (for T-cells) and the bone marrow (for B-cells).

Option C is incorrect: This describes the fundamental action of the Innate Immune System, specifically phagocytosis. Macrophages and neutrophils act as the body’s first line of defence against external pathogens, which has nothing to do with distinguishing “self” from “non-self” tissues.

32

Option D is incorrect: This describes the exact opposite of immune tolerance. The uncontrolled production of autoantibodies against healthy host tissue is the defining pathological mechanism of Autoimmune Diseases.

Additional Facts:

3 Regulatory T-cells (Tregs): These are a highly specialised subpopulation of T-cells. Their exclusive biological function is to suppress immune responses of other cells, acting as the “brakes” of the immune system to maintain peripheral tolerance.

3 Autoimmune Disorders: When peripheral tolerance completely fails, the immune system begins attacking the body’s own organs. This directly results in severe autoimmune diseases such as Rheumatoid Arthritis, Type 1 Diabetes, and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE).

3 Cancer Evasion: Tumours often hijack the mechanism of peripheral immune tolerance to survive. Cancer cells frequently recruit Tregs or express specific inhibitory proteins (like PD-L1) to artificially create a zone of tolerance, effectively blinding the immune system to the growing tumour.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding mitochondria and chloroplasts: 1. Mitochondria and chloroplasts possess their own circular DNA and ribosomes. 2. These organelles can synthesise all their required proteins independently of the nucleus. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Statement 1 is correct: Unlike most other organelles in a eukaryotic cell, mitochondria and chloroplasts possess their own independent genetic machinery. They contain double-stranded, circular DNA molecules, RNA, and their own ribosomes (70S type, which is similar to bacterial ribosomes). This unique feature strongly supports the “Endosymbiotic Theory,” which suggests that these organelles were once free-living bacteria that were engulfed by a larger host cell millions of years ago.

Statement 2 is incorrect: While these organelles do have their own DNA and can synthesise some of their required proteins, they cannot synthesise all of them. They remain heavily dependent on the DNA located within the cell’s main nucleus for the majority of the proteins and enzymes required for their structure and function. Because of this partial dependence, they are accurately classified as semi-autonomous organelles, rather than fully autonomous ones.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Artificial trans fats are highly harmful dietary components that public health agencies are actively eliminating globally. Reason (R): The chemical process of partial hydrogenation creates trans fats, which aggressively raise bad cholesterol and lower good cholesterol. Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
questions.question_type: Assertion and Reason — Standard Relationship Evaluation

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation:
Assertion (A) is true: Artificial trans fats are universally recognised by the World Health Organisation (WHO) as the most dangerous type of dietary fat. Due to their direct link to fatal cardiovascular diseases, global health agencies, including India’s FSSAI, have implemented strict regulations to phase them out of the commercial food supply completely.

Reason (R) is true and explains (A): The extreme harmfulness of trans fats stems directly from their unique chemical structure. They are primarily created through a prolonged industrial process called “partial hydrogenation,” where hydrogen gas is forced into liquid vegetable oils to make them solid at room temperature (like margarine or vanaspati ghee). Biologically, these trans fats are dangerous because they perform a dual negative action: they significantly increase Low-Density Lipoprotein (LDL or “bad” cholesterol) while simultaneously decreasing High-Density Lipoprotein (HDL or “good” cholesterol). Therefore, the Reason perfectly explains the public health Assertion.

Additional facts:

Trans Fats (Artificial & Natural): ◊ Sources: Commercially baked goods, deep-fried street foods, vanaspati ghee, and margarine. (Trace amounts naturally occur in ruminant meat and dairy). ◊ They strictly serve to increase the shelflife of commercial food products. ◊ Problems: The most dangerous fat. Causes severe systemic inflammation, insulin resistance (Type 2 Diabetes), and is a primary driver of coronary artery disease and heart attacks.

Saturated Fats: ◊ Sources: Animal-based products (butter, desi ghee, cheese, red meat) and tropical plant oils (coconut oil, palm oil). They are typically solid at room temperature. ◊ Benefits: Required in small amounts for cellular structure and hormone production. ◊ Problems: Overconsumption can elevate total blood cholesterol levels and LDL (bad) cholesterol, potentially increasing the risk of blockages in arteries. Public health guidelines recommend moderate consumption.

Monounsaturated Fats (MUFAs): ◊ Sources: Olive oil, mustard oil,

33

avocados, almonds, peanuts, and cashews. They are liquid at room temperature but turn cloudy/solid when chilled. ◊ Benefits: Highly beneficial. They actively help lower LDL cholesterol without affecting HDL cholesterol, reduce cellular inflammation, and maintain a healthy cardiovascular system.

Polyunsaturated Fats (PUFAs): ◊ Sources: Sunflower oil, safflower oil, walnuts, flaxseeds, and fatty fish (like salmon and mackerel). ◊ Benefits: Highly beneficial and essential. This group includes Omega-3 and Omega-6 fatty acids, which the human body cannot synthesise on its own. They are critical for brain function, building cell membranes, blood clotting, and fighting systemic inflammation.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the primary mechanism of action of anti-obesity drugs such as Semaglutide?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: It mimics a natural hormone to act on receptors regulating appetite and slowing gastric emptying
options.B: It directly inhibits pancreatic enzymes responsible for the digestion of dietary fats
options.C: It stimulates the central nervous system to markedly increase the basal metabolic rate
options.D: It acts as an osmotic diuretic to promote rapid loss of body water

questions.explanation:
Option A is correct: Semaglutide belongs to a class of medications known as GLP-1 (Glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonists. The human body naturally produces the GLP-1 hormone in the intestines after eating. This medication mimics that exact hormone. It travels to the brain and activates receptors that regulate appetite, making the person feel full much faster and for a longer duration. Additionally, it slows down gastric emptying, meaning food stays in the stomach longer, which drastically reduces overall caloric intake.

Option B is incorrect: This describes the mechanism of older weight-loss drugs like Orlistat. Orlistat works locally in the gut as a lipase inhibitor, preventing the intestines from absorbing about a third of the fat in the food consumed.

Option C is incorrect: This describes the mechanism of stimulant-based appetite suppressants like Phentermine. These drugs trigger the release of neurotransmitters like norepinephrine in the brain, inducing a “fight or flight” response that artificially boosts metabolism and suppresses hunger, often with severe cardiovascular side effects.

Option D is incorrect: This describes the function of diuretics (water pills). While they cause rapid weight loss on the scale by forcing the kidneys to excrete sodium and water, they do not reduce actual body fat and are extremely dangerous if misused for weight management.

Additional Facts:

3 The Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo Nordisk has recently launched this breakthrough weight-loss drug in India under the brand name Wegovy.

3 Drugs like Semaglutide (also sold under the brand name Ozempic) were originally developed and approved strictly for managing Type 2 Diabetes because they stimulate the pancreas to release insulin when blood sugar levels are high.

3 The introduction of these drugs is highly relevant to India’s public health policy, as the country is currently facing a massive epidemic of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs), with obesity acting as the primary catalyst for diabetes and cardiovascular diseases.

questions.q: Which of the following contributions directly enabled James Watson and Francis Crick to propose the double-helix model of DNA in 1953?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: Discovery of DNA polymerase and the mechanism of DNA replication
options.B: X-ray diffraction images of DNA produced by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins
options.C: Radioactive tracer experiments conducted by Hershey and Chase
options.D: Mapping of the human genome through the Human Genome Project

questions.explanation:
In 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the double-helix model for the structure of DNA. However, they did not conduct the foundational laboratory experiments themselves. Their model was primarily based on the vital X-ray crystallography (diffraction) data produced by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins. Franklin’s famous “Photo 51” explicitly revealed the helical nature and fundamental dimensions of the DNA molecule. For this discovery, Watson, Crick, and Wilkins were awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1962 (Rosalind Franklin had passed away, and Nobel prizes are not awarded posthumously).

The discovery of DNA polymerase, the enzyme responsible for synthesising DNA, was made by Arthur Kornberg in 1956, after the double-helix structure had already been proposed.

The Hershey-Chase experiment (1952) used radioactive phosphorus and sulfur to definitively prove that DNA, not protein, was the genetic material entering cells. While historically crucial, it did not reveal the physical structure or shape of the DNA molecule.

The Human Genome Project was an international scientific research project that was launched in 1990 and completed in 2003. It mapped the sequence of nucleotide base pairs.

34

questions.q: Which of the following groups of mRNA codons function as stop codons during protein synthesis?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
During the process of translation (protein synthesis), the cellular machinery “reads” the mRNA sequence in sets of three nucleotides called codons. Out of the 64 possible codons, 61 specifically code for different amino acids.

However, three specific codons, UAA, UAG, and UGA, do not code for any amino acids. Because they do not specify an amino acid, they are referred to as “nonsense” codons. Their primary biological function is to act as a “stop” signal. When the ribosome encounters any of these three codons, it terminates the translation process and releases the newly formed protein chain into the cell.

AUG is actually the universal “start” or initiation codon, which also codes for the amino acid Methionine.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation “mRNA” stand for?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
mRNA stands for Messenger Ribonucleic Acid.

Its primary function is to act as a crucial intermediary in the process of making proteins.

The DNA, which contains the master genetic blueprint, is safely housed inside the cell’s nucleus. However, the actual “factories” that build proteins, the ribosomes, are located outside the nucleus in the cytoplasm.

mRNA is created by copying a specific segment of DNA (a process called transcription). It then carries this genetic “message” out of the nucleus to the ribosomes, dictating the exact sequence of amino acids needed to build a specific protein (a process called translation).

questions.q: Consider the following pairs of specific types of Diabetes and their primary biological characteristics: 1. Type 1 Diabetes: An autoimmune condition where the immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. 2. Type 2 Diabetes: A metabolic disorder characterised by cellular insulin resistance and a gradual decline in natural insulin production. 3. Gestational Diabetes: A temporary form of hyperglycemia that develops exclusively during pregnancy and typically resolves after childbirth. 4. Diabetes Insipidus: A chronic condition caused by excessive dietary sugar intake, leading to dangerously high blood glucose levels. How many pairs of the given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.question_type: Numerical/Calculation — Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Pair 1 is correctly matched: Type 1 Diabetes (formerly known as juvenile-onset diabetes) is strictly an autoimmune disease. The body’s own immune system destroys the beta cells in the pancreas. Consequently, the body produces absolutely zero insulin, making lifelong external insulin administration mandatory for survival.

Pair 2 is correctly matched: Type 2 Diabetes (formerly adult-onset diabetes) is the most common form globally. It is heavily driven by lifestyle factors, genetics, and obesity. The body still produces insulin, but the liver, muscle, and fat cells become “resistant” to it. Over time, the pancreas cannot make enough insulin to overcome this resistance.

Pair 3 is correctly matched: Gestational Diabetes occurs when pregnancy hormones interfere with the body’s ability to use insulin effectively, leading to temporary insulin resistance. While blood sugar levels usually return to normal shortly after delivery, it significantly increases the mother’s future risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes.

Pair 4 is incorrectly matched: Diabetes Insipidus has absolutely nothing to do with blood sugar (glucose) or dietary sugar intake. It is a completely separate and rare disorder of fluid regulation. It is caused by a deficiency of, or insensitivity to, the antidiuretic hormone (ADH or vasopressin), which leads to extreme thirst and massive volumes of dilute urine.

Additional Facts:

3 HbA1c Test: This is the gold-standard diagnostic blood test for diabetes. It measures the percentage of blood sugar attached to haemoglobin, providing an average of the patient’s blood glucose levels over the past 2 to 3 months.

3 The Role of Insulin: Insulin is a peptide hormone produced by the pancreas. Its primary biological function is to unlock cells, allowing glucose from the bloodstream to enter and be used for cellular energy.

3 Public Health Crisis: India is frequently referred to as the “Diabetes Capital of the World.” The prevalence of Type 2 Diabetes is escalating rapidly, driven by rapid urbanization, shifting dietary patterns towards processed foods, and increasingly sedentary lifestyles.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding meiosis: 1. Meiosis is termed reduction division because it reduces the chromosome number by half in gametes, thereby maintaining the chromosome number of the species after fertilisation. 2. Meiosis generates genetic variation through the exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Statement 1 is correct: Human somatic (body) cells are diploid, meaning they contain 46 chromosomes (23 pairs). If gametes (sperm and egg) were produced through regular cell division (mitosis), they would also contain 46 chromosomes. Upon fertilisation, the resulting offspring would end up with 92 chromosomes, fundamentally altering the species. Meiosis solves this by acting as a reduction division. It reduces the chromosome number by exactly half, creating haploid gametes containing only 23 single chromosomes. When a sperm and egg fuse during fertilisation, the normal diploid number of 46 is perfectly restored in the zygote.

35

Statement 2 is correct: Meiosis is the primary biological engine of genetic diversity in sexually reproducing organisms. During the first phase of meiosis (specifically Prophase I), paired homologous chromosomes align closely together and physically swap segments of their DNA. This phenomenon is known as “crossing over” or genetic recombination. Because of this exchange, the four resulting gametes are genetically unique from one another and from the parent cell. This ensures that no two children from the same parents are exactly alike (excluding identical twins), providing a critical foundation for evolutionary adaptation and survival.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the ‘Project Akashteer’ system: 1. It is a fully indigenous, automated Air Defence Control System developed by the DRDO and HAL. 2. It is a vehicle-based, mobile component of the C4ISR framework designed to automate threat tracking. 3. It signifies a strategic military shift from proactive retaliation toward a static, passive defence posture. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Statement 1 is incorrect: While it is a fully indigenous and highly automated Air Defence Control and Reporting System, it was strictly developed by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), but DRDO and ISRO also contributed to its development.

Statement 2 is correct: Akashteer is an integral part of the modern C4ISR (Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance) framework. It is specifically designed as a vehicle-based system. This high mobility allows the Indian Army to rapidly deploy and reposition the control centres during active combat.

Statement 3 is incorrect: Project Akashteer reflects the exact opposite strategic shift. By leveraging AI to seamlessly link various radar nodes and firing units, it enables a shift from passive, isolated defence monitoring to highly coordinated, proactive retaliation against hostile drones, rockets, and aircraft.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best defines Gregor Mendel’s “Law of Independent Assortment”?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: The two alleles of a trait separate during gamete formation so that each gamete receives only one allele.
options.B: The inheritance of one trait is independent of the inheritance of another trait.
options.C: A dominant allele masks the expression of a recessive allele in a heterozygote.
options.D: Genes located close together on the same chromosome are inherited together.

questions.explanation:
Option A is incorrect: This statement describes Mendel’s Law of Segregation (also known as the purity of gametes). It explains that allele pairs separate or segregate during gamete formation, meaning a sperm or egg carries only one allele for each inherited trait.

Option B is correct: Mendel’s Law of Independent Assortment states that when two or more pairs of traits are considered, the segregation of one pair of traits is entirely independent of the other pair of traits during the formation of gametes. For example, the gene determining a pea plant’s seed colour (yellow or green) is passed on to the offspring independently of the gene determining its seed shape (round or wrinkled). Mendel derived this principle from his famous dihybrid cross experiments.

Option C is incorrect: This statement describes the Law of Dominance, which explains why some traits are expressed over others in a hybrid organism.

Option D is incorrect: This statement describes Genetic Linkage. Linkage was discovered later by Thomas Hunt Morgan and is an exception to Mendel’s Law of Independent Assortment. Genes located very close together on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together and do not assort independently.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a component of the indigenous Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS) framework?

questions.explanation:
