questions.q: Which of the following pairs regarding naval warship classes and their operational roles is incorrectly matched?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: Destroyers: Fast, heavily armed multi-role fleet escorts capable of defending against air, surface and submarine threats
options.B: Cruisers: Warships designed exclusively for amphibious landings and deployment of marine expeditionary forces
options.C: Frigates: Medium-sized warships commonly optimised for anti-submarine warfare and convoy protection
options.D: Corvettes: Small warships generally used for coastal defence, patrol and fast attack roles

questions.explanation:
Pair 1 is correctly matched: Destroyers are the heavily armed workhorses of modern blue-water navies. They are fast, highly manoeuvrable escorts that provide a comprehensive defensive “shield” (Anti-Air, Anti-Submarine, and Anti-Surface) around highly valuable, vulnerable assets like Aircraft Carriers.

Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The description provided belongs to Amphibious Assault Ships (such as Landing Helicopter Docks - LHDs), not Cruisers. Cruisers are the largest and most powerful traditional surface combatant ships in active service today (excluding aircraft carriers). They are capable of operating completely independently or leading their own maritime task forces.

Pair 3 is correctly matched: Frigates are a step below destroyers in size, armament, and speed. While modern stealth frigates possess multi-role capabilities, their foundational naval doctrine has always prioritised Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) and escorting unarmed merchant fleets through hostile waters.

Pair 4 is correctly matched: Corvettes are the smallest recognised class of true warships. Because they carry less fuel and fewer supplies, they lack the extreme endurance of frigates or destroyers. Therefore, they are optimised for “brown-water” or littoral (coastal) operations, fast strikes, and policing a nation’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).

Additional Fact:

3 To understand modern naval fleets, surface combatants generally follow this tonnage/size hierarchy (from largest to smallest): Cruiser > Destroyer > Frigate > Corvette > Fast Attack Craft/Patrol Boat.

3 Project 15B (Visakhapatnam Class): This is the Indian Navy’s latest and most lethal class of indigenous stealth guided-missile Destroyers, built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL). It includes INS Visakhapatnam, INS Mormugao, INS Imphal, and INS Surat.

3 Project 17A (Nilgiri Class): This represents India’s ongoing program to construct highly advanced, radar-evading stealth Frigates.

3 Project 28 (Kamorta Class): These are India’s indigenously built Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) Corvettes. Because their primary job is hunting submarines, they are specifically built using special high-tensile steel to minimise their underwater acoustic signature (noise).

questions.q: Consider the following technological applications: 1. Targeted drug delivery 2. Heavy metal water purification 3. Quantum dot displays 4. Self-cleaning fabrics 5. Smart packaging for agriculture Which of the above are recognised applications of nanotechnology?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Nanotechnology is highly interdisciplinary, and all five of the listed fields heavily utilise nanoscale materials (typically between 1 and 100 nanometers) to achieve revolutionary results.

Targeted drug delivery (Medicine): Nanoparticles are engineered to carry pharmaceutical drugs directly to diseased cells (such as targeted chemotherapy for cancer tumours), which drastically minimises toxic side effects on surrounding healthy tissues.

Heavy metal water purification (Environment): Nanomaterials, particularly carbon nanotubes and magnetic nanoparticles, are highly effective at absorbing, filtering, and neutralising toxic heavy metals and microscopic pathogens from industrial wastewater.

Quantum dot displays (Electronics): Modern QLED televisions and monitors utilise nanocrystals known as “quantum dots” that emit specific, highly vibrant colours when illuminated, resulting in superior image quality and energy efficiency.

Self-cleaning fabrics (Textiles): Everyday textiles and industrial fabrics coated with nanoparticles (like titanium dioxide or zinc oxide) become highly hydrophobic. They actively repel water, resist deep stains, and kill odour-causing bacteria.

Smart packaging for agriculture (Food/Agri): Nanosensors integrated directly into food packaging can actively monitor the environment, detect early bacterial growth, and alert consumers to spoilage, vastly extending shelf life and reducing food waste.

Additional Facts:

37

3 Graphene: This is one of the most famous nanomaterials. It is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a 2D hexagonal lattice. It is highly prized for being roughly 200 times stronger than steel while remaining highly flexible and an exceptional conductor of electricity.

3 India’s Nano Mission: To promote domestic research and capacity building, the Government of India launched the umbrella “Nano Mission” (National Mission on Nano Science and Technology) in 2007, spearheaded by the Department of Science and Technology (DST).

3 The “Bottom-Up” Approach: Nanomanufacturing often uses a bottomup approach, where complex materials and devices are built molecule by molecule, or atom by atom, allowing for unprecedented structural precision.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs regarding genetic disorders and their associated inheritance patterns or chromosomal abnormalities: 1. Haemophilia : X-linked recessive trait 2. Sickle-cell anaemia : Autosomal recessive trait 3. Down’s syndrome : Monosomy of chromosome 21 4. Klinefelter’s syndrome : 44 Autosomes + XO Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Pair 1 is correctly matched: Haemophilia is a classic X-linked recessive disorder. Because it is carried on the X chromosome, it predominantly affects males (who have only one X chromosome), while females act as carriers unless both of their X chromosomes carry the defective gene.

Pair 2 is correctly matched: Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive trait. It is controlled by a single pair of alleles on the autosomes (non-sex chromosomes). It can be transmitted from parents to offspring when both partners are carrier for the gene (heterozygous).

Pair 3 is incorrectly matched: Down syndrome is not a monosomy. It is caused by the presence of an additional copy of chromosome number 21. This condition is scientifically referred to as Trisomy 21.

Pair 4 is incorrectly matched: Klinefelter’s syndrome is caused by the presence of an additional copy of the X chromosome in males, resulting in a karyotype of 47 chromosomes (44 Autosomes + XXY). The genetic makeup of “44 Autosomes + XO” (absence of one X chromosome) actually describes Turner’s syndrome in females.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding fighter aircraft generations are correct? 1. Second-generation fighters marked the emergence of supersonic capability along with early radar and guided air-to-air missiles. 2. Third-generation fighters increasingly adopted multi-role roles and introduced Beyond Visual Range combat capability. 3. Fourth-generation fighters are associated with fly-by-wire systems and enhanced aerodynamic manoeuvrability. 4. Fifth-generation fighters are primarily defined by dependence on ramjet engines for sustained hypersonic flight. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Statement 1 is correct: Second-generation fighters (developed in the 1950s and 60s) broke the sound barrier in level flight. This generation introduced airborne radar systems and the first infrared-guided missiles (like the AIM-9 Sidewinder). Example: MiG-21.

Statement 2 is correct: Third-generation fighters (1960s and 70s) were designed as multi-role aircraft capable of both air superiority and ground attack. They heavily utilised improved radar to fire BVR (Beyond Visual Range) missiles. Example: F-4 Phantom and MiG-23.

Statement 3 is correct: Fourth-generation fighters (1970s to 1990s) combat with “fly-bywire” computers. Instead of mechanical pulleys, computers interpreted the pilot’s inputs, allowing jets to be aerodynamically unstable but incredibly agile and manoeuvrable. Examples: F-16, Su-27, Mirage 2000.

Statement 4 is incorrect: Fifth-generation fighters do not rely on ramjets for hypersonic flight. The defining characteristics of a 5th-generation jet are Stealth (Very Low Observable radar cross-section), Sensor Fusion (computers combining all sensor data into a single battlespace picture), and Supercruise (the ability to fly at supersonic speeds without using fuel-guzzling afterburners). Examples: F-22 Raptor, F-35 Lightning II, Su-57, and China’s J-20.

Additional Facts:

3 The “4.5 Generation”: Because 5th-generation stealth jets are overwhelmingly expensive to develop and maintain, many air forces rely on 4.5-generation jets. These are essentially highly upgraded 4th-gen airframes fitted with 5th-gen electronics, specifically AESA (Active Electronically Scanned Array) radars.

3 The Indian Air Force’s Rafale and the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk-1A perfectly represent 4.5-generation capabilities.

3 Project AMCA: India is actively developing its own indigenous 5th-generation stealth fighter under the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) program, spearheaded by the DRDO and HAL.

3 First Generation: For context, 1st-generation fighters were the earliest subsonic jet aircraft of the Korean War era, entirely lacking radar and relying solely on unguided machine guns and cannons. Example: F-86 Sabre and MiG-15.

questions.q: Which of the following principles is primarily utilised by the Hyperloop transportation system to achieve very high speeds?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: Aerodynamic lift combined with jet propulsion
options.C: Positive pneumatic pressure pushing a pod through a pipeline
options.D: Superconducting cables carrying high-voltage direct current

questions.explanation:
The Hyperloop is a proposed ultra-high-speed ground transportation system. It relies on two

38

primary physical principles. First, it uses magnetic levitation (maglev) to float the passenger pods, completely eliminating rolling friction with the track. Second, the pods travel through a sealed network of tubes where powerful pumps remove almost all the air to create a near-vacuum (lowpressure environment). This virtually eliminates aerodynamic drag (air resistance), allowing the pods to glide at airline speeds (up to 1,000+ km/h) using very little electrical energy.

This describes the fundamental operational mechanics of a standard commercial jet airliner flying in the upper atmosphere, not a ground-based tube transport system.

This describes a traditional pneumatic tube system (like the ones historically used in banks or post offices to send small capsules). Hyperloop uses a vacuum (pulling air out) rather than positive pressure (pushing air in) to achieve its speeds.

While superconducting cables are used in advanced power grids and some maglev systems, simply carrying high-voltage current does not describe the physical propulsion and drag-reduction mechanism that defines the Hyperloop.

Additional Facts:

3 The “Fifth Mode” of Transport: The modern Hyperloop concept was first proposed in a 2013 white paper by Elon Musk (CEO of SpaceX and Tesla), who famously described it as the “fifth mode of transport” alongside planes, trains, cars, and boats.

3 NITI Aayog has actively explored the technological and commercial viability of Hyperloop in India. Previously, Virgin Hyperloop had proposed a flagship route connecting Mumbai and Pune, which aimed to reduce the 3-hour journey to roughly 25 minutes.

3 Because the system overcomes the two biggest barriers to high-speed travel (air resistance and ground friction), it requires a fraction of the energy per passenger compared to a jet aircraft. If the system is powered by solar panels mounted along the top of the tubes, it could potentially be a completely carbonneutral transit system.

questions.q: Which of the following cellular structures is primarily responsible for the synthesis of proteins by translating messenger RNA (mRNA)?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Ribosomes are dense, granular structures found in all living cells, including both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. They serve as the indispensable “protein factories” of the cell. During the process of translation, ribosomes attach to messenger RNA (mRNA) and read its genetic instructions. They then facilitate the linking of specific amino acids in the correct sequence to form long polypeptide chains, which ultimately fold into functional proteins.

Golgi apparatus functions as the cellular post office. It is primarily responsible for modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for delivery to other targeted destinations.

Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell, responsible for generating cellular energy in the form of ATP through the process of cellular respiration.

Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) completely lacks ribosomes on its surface. It is primarily involved in the synthesis of lipids (fats), steroid hormones, and the detoxification of harmful chemicals, rather than protein synthesis.

questions.q: Which of the following aviation devices records flight data and cockpit conversations, and helps in accident investigation after a crash?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
The Black Box (which actually consists of the Flight Data Recorder and Cockpit Voice Recorder) is heavily armoured to survive crashes and records all mechanical flight parameters and cockpit audio for accident investigation. It is painted bright orange and equipped with an underwater locator beacon.

A Ground Proximity Warning System (GPWS) is an active instrument that alerts pilots if the aircraft is in immediate danger of flying into the ground.

Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) communicates with the transponders of other nearby aircraft to prevent mid-air collisions.

The Flight Management Computer (FMC) is the “brain” of the navigation system that automates inflight tasks, but it is not armoured to survive a crash or record flight history for investigations.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes altermagnetism, a newly identified magnetic phase?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: They exhibit a strong, uniform magnetic field that attracts magnetic materials
options.B: They possess zero net magnetisation but can exhibit spin-polarised electronic behaviour
options.C: They are permanent magnets that lose magnetism at room temperature
options.D: They completely expel external magnetic fields and exhibit levitation

questions.explanation:
Altermagnetism is a recently confirmed third fundamental class of magnetism. It essentially combines the best features of the two traditional classes. Like antiferromagnets, altermagnets have no net macroscopic magnetic field (meaning they don’t stick to the fridge and don’t create stray fields). However, due to their unique crystal symmetries, they still exhibit strong “spin-polarised” electron bands, a useful property previously thought to belong almost exclusively to ferromagnets

39

Additional Facts:

3 The Spintronics Revolution: Standard electronics use the charge of an electron to process data. “Spintronics” aims to use the spin of an electron to create vastly faster and more energy-efficient computers. Altermagnets are considered a “holy grail” for spintronics because their lack of a net magnetic field means tightly packed computer chips won’t interfere with each other, while their spin-polarisation allows data to be carried effectively.

3 While theorised a few years earlier, the existence of altermagnets was definitively proven in early 2024 by international researchers using advanced X-ray spectroscopy at facilities like the Swiss Light Source (SLS).

3 Candidate Materials: Common materials proven to exhibit altermagnetism include Manganese telluride and Ruthenium dioxide.

questions.q: Which of the following substances or organisms is NOT classified as an agricultural “Biostimulant”?
questions.question_type: Negative/Exception MCQ — Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Glyphosate is a highly controversial, broadspectrum synthetic herbicide. Its primary biological function is to kill unwanted weeds and grasses by inhibiting a specific plant enzyme pathway. It does not stimulate plant growth or improve crop health.

Humic and fulvic acids are complex organic molecules found naturally in soil. When applied to crops, they act as powerful biostimulants by significantly improving the soil structure, increasing root mass, and enhancing the plant’s ability to absorb vital nutrients.

Seaweed extracts (commonly derived from brown algae like Ascophyllum nodosum) are heavily used as biostimulants. They are rich in natural plant hormones (like auxins and cytokinins) that actively promote cellular division and build the plant’s resilience against abiotic stresses like extreme heat or drought.

Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi (AMF) are highly beneficial soil microorganisms. They form a symbiotic relationship with plant roots, effectively acting as an extension of the root system to help the plant scavenge for water and difficult-to-absorb nutrients like phosphorus.

Additional Facts:

3 In a major agricultural reform, the Government of India amended the Fertiliser (Inorganic, Organic or Mixed) (Control) Order (FCO) in 2021 to officially recognise “Biostimulants” as a distinct, regulated category of agricultural inputs for the first time.

3 It is crucial for regulatory and examination purposes to understand that biostimulants are entirely distinct from Fertilizers (which directly provide bulk nutrients like NPK) and Pesticides (which directly kill pests or diseases). Biostimulants operate by enhancing the plant’s natural physiological processes.

3 The promotion of biostimulants is a core component of India’s push towards natural farming and sustainable agriculture, aiming to reduce the excessive reliance on harmful chemical fertilisers and boost long-term soil health.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the primary function of lysosomes and their hydrolytic enzymes?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: They act as the primary site for the continuous synthesis of cellular proteins.
options.B: They capture solar energy to produce chemical energy for the cell.
options.C: They modify, sort, and package lipids for transport outside the cell membrane.
options.D: They serve as a cellular waste disposal system by digesting worn-out organelles and foreign materials.

questions.explanation:
Lysosomes act as the primary waste disposal system of the cell. They are membrane-bound sacs filled with powerful digestive enzymes (hydrolytic enzymes) capable of breaking down complex organic materials. They help keep the cell clean by actively digesting any foreign material that enters the cell, such as harmful bacteria or food particles, as well as breaking down old, poorly functioning cellular organelles.

During a disturbance in cellular metabolism, for example, when the cell gets damaged, lysosomes may burst, and the enzymes digest their own cell. Therefore, lysosomes are also popularly known as the “suicide bags” of a cell.

questions.q: Which specialised branch of anatomy is dedicated to the scientific study of the structure and function of bones?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Osteology (derived from the Greek words osteon, meaning “bone”, and logos meaning “study”) is the specialised branch of gross anatomy, physical anthropology, and palaeontology dedicated to the scientific study of bones, skeletal elements, teeth, microbone morphology, and the ossification process.

Myology: This is the scientific study of the muscular system, including the structure, function, and diseases of muscles.

Cytology: This is the branch of biology concerned with the study of the structure, chemistry, and function of individual plant and animal cells.

Histology: Also known as microscopic anatomy, this is the study of the microscopic structure of biological tissues.

40

Additional Facts:

3 Bones are not static; they are highly dynamic living tissues continuously being remodelled. This process is governed primarily by two types of cells: Osteoblasts (which actively build new bone tissue) and Osteoclasts (which break down and resorb old or damaged bone).

3 Bone Composition: Chemically, bone tissue is a composite material made of an organic matrix (primarily flexible collagen fibres) and inorganic mineral salts (primarily calcium phosphate in a crystalline arrangement called hydroxyapatite), which provides immense compressive strength.

questions.q: Which of the following organisms is unique for having haemoglobin dissolved directly in its blood plasma while lacking red blood cells (RBCs)?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: In an Earthworm (an annelid), the respiratory pigment hemoglobin is not contained within specialized red blood cells (RBCs) as it is in vertebrates. Instead, the hemoglobin is dissolved directly into the blood plasma.

questions.q: Which mosquito genus is identified by its characteristic resting posture, with the body held at an angle to the surface?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Anopheles mosquitoes are morphologically distinguished in the field by their unique resting posture. When they land on a surface, adults rest with their heads down and their abdomens pointing upward at a distinct angle (often around 45 degrees). In contrast, most other common mosquito genera, including Culex and Aedes, rest with their bodies positioned roughly parallel to the surface.

questions.q: Fungi are classified separately from plants primarily due to the absence of which of the following?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Unlike plants, fungi entirely lack chlorophyll. Because they do not possess this pigment, they cannot perform photosynthesis to produce their own food (autotrophy). Instead, fungi are heterotrophs, meaning they must absorb their nutrients from other living or dead organic matter.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the endoplasmic reticulum in eukaryotic cells: 1. Rough endoplasmic reticulum appears rough due to the presence of ribosomes on its surface and is associated with protein synthesis. 2. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum lacks ribosomes and is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification in liver cells. Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.question_type: Negative/Exception MCQ — Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Statement 1 is correct: The Endoplasmic Reticulum is a large network of membrane-bound tubes and sheets. The Rough ER (RER) looks rough under an electron microscope because it has particles called ribosomes attached to its surface. Since ribosomes are the “protein factories” of the cell, the RER is fundamentally involved in synthesising and modifying proteins, which are then sent to various places in the cell depending on need.

Statement 2 is correct: The Smooth ER (SER) does not have ribosomes attached to it, hence its smooth appearance. Its primary cellular function is the synthesis of essential lipids and steroid hormones. Furthermore, in the liver cells of vertebrates, the SER plays a vital, specialised role in detoxifying many harmful metabolic by-products, drugs, and external poisons.

questions.q: What term denotes the functional role of an organism within its ecosystem?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
An ecological niche refers to the specific functional role or “profession” an organism plays within its ecosystem. It encompasses everything an organism does to survive and reproduce, including what it eats, what eats it, its behaviour, how it alters the environment, and its interactions with both living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) factors.

A biome is a massive geographical area characterised by its climate and the dominant vegetation and animal life found there (e.g., Tundra, Tropical Rainforest, Desert).

An ecotone is a transition zone or boundary area where two different biological communities or ecosystems meet and integrate (e.g., a marshland between a river and a forest, or an estuary where freshwater meets the ocean). Ecotones usually have high biodiversity.

Ecological succession is the gradual, predictable process by which the structure of a biological community changes and evolves over time, often following a disturbance like a forest fire or volcanic eruption.

Habitat vs. Niche: A classic ecological analogy is that a habitat is an organism’s “address” (where it lives), while a niche is its “profession” (what it does for a living).

questions.q: Which of the following represents a mutualistic association between algae and fungi?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
A Lichen is not a single organism, but rather a remarkable mutualistic association between two distinct entities: a fungus (the mycobiont) and a photosynthetic partner, either an alga or a cyanobacterium (the phycobiont). In this symbiotic relationship, the fungus provides a protective physical structure, gathers moisture, and extracts minerals from the surrounding environment. In

41

return, the photosynthetic partner, whether an alga or a cyanobacterium, both of which contain chlorophyll and are capable of photosynthesis, produces carbohydrates that sustain both organisms.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the primary function of the Golgi apparatus in a living cell?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: Generating cellular energy in the form of ATP molecules
options.B: Modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for delivery
options.C: Destroying old, worn-out cell organelles and foreign bacteria
options.D: Storing genetic information and controlling the process of cell division

questions.explanation:
The Golgi apparatus (or Golgi complex) functions very much like the “post office” or packaging and dispatch centre of the cell. Materials that are synthesised near the Endoplasmic Reticulum (such as proteins and lipids) are sent to the Golgi apparatus.

Here, these materials are chemically modified, carefully sorted, and packaged into small membranebound sacs (vesicles). They are then dispatched to various target destinations either inside the cell or secreted outside the cell membrane.

questions.q: What is the term for the mutualistic association between fungi and plant roots?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Mycorrhiza (plural: mycorrhizae) refers to the mutually beneficial (symbiotic) association between a specialised soil fungus and the roots of a vascular plant. In this relationship, the fungal hyphae vastly extend the root system’s surface area, helping the plant absorb difficult-to-reach water and essential minerals (especially phosphorus). In return, the plant provides the fungus with carbohydrates (sugars) produced through photosynthesis.

Parasitism: This is a relationship where one organism (the parasite) benefits at the direct expense and harm of the other organism (the host), such as a tick on a dog or a tapeworm in an intestine.

Saprophytism: This refers to organisms (like many decomposer fungi and bacteria) that obtain their nutrients by breaking down dead and decaying organic matter, rather than interacting with living plant roots.

Commensalism: This is an ecological interaction where one species benefits while the other is completely unaffected (neither helped nor harmed). An example is a bird building a nest in a large tree.

questions.q: What are organisms that break down dead organic matter into simpler inorganic substances called?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Decomposers (primarily bacteria and fungi) are organisms that break down complex, dead, and decaying organic matter into simpler inorganic substances like carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus. They secrete specialized enzymes into their environment to break down the organic material externally before absorbing the nutrients. This process cleans the environment and recycles essential nutrients back into the soil and atmosphere for plants to use again.

questions.q: Which of the following forms the basis of organoid intelligence, an emerging approach to biological computing?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Organoid intelligence (OI) is a revolutionary multidisciplinary field that uses 3D cultures of human brain cells, known as brain organoids, as biological hardware for computing. Instead of relying on traditional rigid silicon microchips, OI seeks to harness the complex processing power, structural plasticity, and extreme energy efficiency of living biological neural networks to perform computational memory and learning tasks.

questions.q: Charles Darwin is associated with which of the following evolutionary concepts?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Charles Darwin is fundamentally associated with the concept of Natural Selection. He introduced this mechanism of evolution in his groundbreaking 1859 book, On the Origin of Species. Natural selection is the process by which organisms better adapted to their environment tend to survive and produce more offspring.

Inheritance of Acquired Characters: Proposed by Jean-Baptiste Lamarck. This theory (often called Lamarckism) suggested that organisms could pass down physical traits acquired during their lifetime to their offspring (e.g., a giraffe stretching its neck to reach high leaves would pass a longer neck to its babies).

Mutation Theory: Proposed by Hugo de Vries. He suggested that new species arise from sudden, large, and unpredictable genetic changes (mutations) rather than gradual, continuous variations.

Germplasm Theory: Proposed by August Weismann. This theory states that heritable information is transmitted only by germ cells (sperm and egg) in the gonads, and that changes to somatic (body) cells cannot be passed on to offspring, effectively disproving Lamarckism.

questions.q: Which technique uses cosmic-ray subatomic particles to image the internal structure of large solid objects without physical damage?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Muon tomography (or muography) is a revolutionary imaging technique that uses naturally occurring muons, which are heavy, high-energy

42

subatomic particles created when cosmic rays collide with the Earth’s upper atmosphere. Because muons are much heavier than electrons, they can easily pass through hundreds of meters of solid rock or dense metal. By placing detectors around a large structure to track how many muons pass through, scientists can create a 3D “X-ray” of its interior.

Carbon dating: This is a radiometric dating method used to determine the exact age of organic materials (like ancient wood or bones) based on the decay of the Carbon-14 isotope. It does not image internal structures.

LiDAR scanning: Light Detection and Ranging uses pulsed lasers to map external surface topography with high precision. It is excellent for finding ruins hidden under dense jungle canopies, but it cannot see through solid stone.

Seismic refraction: This technique uses controlled acoustic shockwaves (like small explosives or heavy thumping) to map underground geological layers based on how sound waves bend.

Additional Facts:

3 ScanPyramids Project: In 2017, muon tomography made global headlines when it was used to discover a massive, previously unknown hidden void (chamber) deep inside the Great Pyramid of Giza without moving a single stone.

3 Because the technique is entirely passive and doesn’t require humans to enter dangerous areas, it was crucially deployed at the highly radioactive Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant in Japan to safely locate the melted nuclear fuel cores.

3 National Security: Modern border security agencies are increasingly exploring muon scanners for cargo ports to detect shielded nuclear contraband or heavy metals hidden inside shipping containers that standard X-rays cannot penetrate.

questions.q: Which process uses microorganisms such as Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans to extract metals from low-grade ores through bioleaching?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Biomining is a highly sustainable metallurgical technique that utilises specialised extremophile microorganisms (most commonly Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans) to extract valuable metals like copper, gold, and uranium from low-grade ores. In a process called “bioleaching,” these bacteria essentially feed on the sulfur and iron binding the rock, oxidising the minerals and dissolving the trapped metals into a liquid solution that can be easily collected and purified.

Bioprinting: This involves using 3D printing technology equipped with “bio-ink” (living cells) to construct complex biological tissues or artificial organs layer by layer.

Biostimulation: This is a bioremediation technique where nutrients (like phosphorus or nitrogen) are added to a contaminated environment (like an oil spill) to stimulate the rapid growth of naturally occurring, pollution-eating microbes.

Bioaugmentation: This is the practice of artificially introducing specifically cultured laboratory strains of bacteria into a contaminated site to speed up the degradation of complex pollutants.

Additional Facts:

3 Urban Mining (E-Waste): Biomining is heavily researched today as an eco-friendly alternative to chemical smelting for extracting precious metals (gold, silver, palladium) from electronic waste (e-waste) circuit boards.

3 Swachh Bharat Mission Context: While scientifically biomining refers to metal extraction, in Indian civic administration and the Swachh Bharat Mission, “biomining” is the official term used for the bioremediation and mechanical segregation of massive legacy waste in old urban landfills (like Ghazipur in Delhi) to reclaim the land.

3 Cost and Energy Efficiency: Traditional smelting requires massive furnaces and vast amounts of coal/electricity, producing heavy carbon emissions. Biomining operates at near room temperature and relies entirely on biological processes, drastically reducing the carbon footprint of the mining industry.

questions.q: Edward Jenner developed the world’s first successful vaccine against:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
In 1796, the English physician Edward Jenner developed the world’s first successful vaccine, which was designed to combat smallpox. He made a crucial historical observation that milkmaids who had previously contracted cowpox (a relatively mild disease) were naturally immune to the highly contagious and deadly smallpox virus. He tested this by deliberately inoculating a young boy with material from a cowpox sore, which successfully provided the boy with immunity against smallpox. This revolutionary concept eventually led to the complete global eradication of smallpox, certified by the WHO in 1980.

Polio: The first successful polio vaccine was developed by Jonas Salk in the 1950s.

43

Rabies: The first vaccine for rabies was pioneered by Louis Pasteur in 1885.

Tuberculosis: The BCG vaccine for tuberculosis was developed by Albert Calmette and Camille Guérin in 1921.

questions.q: What is the term for transplantation of live cells, tissues or organs from a non-human animal into a human recipient?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Xenotransplantation is the surgical procedure involving the transplantation, implantation, or infusion into a human recipient of live cells, tissues, or organs from a non-human animal source.

Autotransplantation: This involves transplanting tissue from one part of a person’s own body to another part (e.g., skin grafts for burns or bone marrow transplants using the patient’s own stem cells).

Allotransplantation: This is the most common type of transplant. It involves transplanting organs or tissues from one human to another non-genetically identical human (e.g., a standard kidney or heart transplant from a donor).

Isotransplantation: Also known as syngeneic transplantation, this refers to a transplant between two genetically identical individuals, such as identical (monozygotic) twins.

Additional Facts:

3 The Porcine Solution: Genetically modified pigs are currently the primary candidates for xenotransplantation. Their organs are remarkably similar in size and physiological function to human organs.

3 Hyperacute Rejection: The biggest historical hurdle to xenotransplantation was the human immune system instantly attacking the animal organ. To solve this, scientists use CRISPR gene-editing to remove the alpha-gal sugar gene from pigs (a sugar found in most mammals, but not humans), which normally triggers this violent immune response.

3 Zoonotic Disease Risk: A major ethical and biological concern surrounding xenotransplantation is the risk of “xenozoonosis”—the possibility of transmitting animal viruses, specifically Porcine Endogenous Retroviruses (PERVs), into the broader human population.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the phenomenon of quantum tunnelling?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: The ability of a quantum system to exist in multiple states simultaneously until measurement
options.B: Instantaneous transfer of a quantum state between physically separated particles
options.C: Passage of a subatomic particle through an energy barrier despite lacking sufficient classical energy to overcome it
options.D: Loss of a quantum state due to interaction with the external environment

questions.explanation:
Quantum tunnelling is a fundamental quantum mechanical phenomenon. It occurs when a subatomic particle (like an electron) passes through a physical or potential energy barrier. Classically, the particle does not possess enough kinetic energy to surmount this barrier. However, due to its wave-like nature, there is a strict mathematical probability that it will “tunnel” directly through to the other side.

Quantum Superposition is the principle that allows a quantum computer’s qubits to represent both 0 and 1 at the exact same time, providing massive parallel processing power.

Quantum Entanglement refers to two or more particles becoming intrinsically linked. The physical measurement of one instantly dictates the state of the other, regardless of spatial distance.

Quantum Decoherence is the primary technological obstacle in quantum computing. It occurs when minor environmental noise (like heat or electromagnetic waves) destroys the quantum state, causing the system to revert to classical binary states and lose its computational advantage.

Additional Facts:

3 Stellar Nuclear Fusion: Quantum tunnelling is the exact physical mechanism that powers the Sun. It allows hydrogen protons to overcome their mutual electrostatic repulsion and fuse together at core temperatures that are classically too low for fusion.

3 Modern Electronics: The phenomenon is actively utilised in everyday consumer electronics. Solid-state drives (SSDs) and USB flash memory drives use quantum tunnelling to erase and rewrite data across insulating oxide layers.

3 Scanning Tunnelling Microscope (STM): This advanced scientific instrument uses the tunnelling of electrons between a sharp metallic tip and a conducting surface to image materials at the individual atomic level.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding lymphocytes in the human immune system: 1. B-lymphocytes are primarily responsible for cell-mediated immunity by directly destroying infected and tumour cells. 2. T-lymphocytes do not secrete antibodies but assist B-lymphocytes in antibody production. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_type: Negative/Exception MCQ — Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Statement 1 is incorrect: B-lymphocytes are responsible for humoral immunity (antibodymediated immunity), not cell-mediated immunity. When they encounter a pathogen, they produce an army of specialised proteins called antibodies that circulate in the blood plasma to neutralise the threat. It is actually the Cytotoxic (Killer) T-cells that are responsible for cell-mediated immunity, directly attacking the body’s own cells that have become infected by viruses or turned cancerous.

44

Statement 2 is correct: T-lymphocytes fundamentally differ from B-cells because they never produce antibodies themselves. However, a specific subset called “Helper T-cells” acts as the command centre of the immune response. When they detect an infection, they release chemical signals (cytokines) that actively stimulate and “help” the B-lymphocytes to start producing antibodies. Without Helper T-cells, B-cells cannot effectively mount an antibody response.

questions.q: Which experimental device uses powerful magnetic fields to confine hot plasma in a toroidal chamber for controlled nuclear fusion?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Tokamak is an experimental machine designed to harness the energy of nuclear fusion. The core of a tokamak is a doughnut-shaped (toroidal) vacuum chamber. Because the plasma (superheated gas) inside must reach temperatures over 100 million degrees Celsius, much hotter than the centre of the Sun, and no solid material can contain it. Therefore, the Tokamak uses incredibly powerful magnetic coils to confine the plasma in mid-air, preventing it from touching the walls.

Additional Facts:

3 ITER (International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor): This is the world’s largest tokamak, currently under construction in southern France. It is a massive international collaboration involving 35 nations, including India, aiming to prove the feasibility of fusion as a large-scale, safe, and carbon-free energy source.

3 The Fourth State of Matter: To achieve fusion, gases are heated to extreme temperatures until they become plasma. In a plasma, electrons are entirely stripped from the atomic nuclei, making it highly electrically conductive and susceptible to magnetic fields.

3 Abundant Fuel: Unlike nuclear fission (which splits heavy, radioactive elements like Uranium), fusion combines light elements. It primarily uses isotopes of hydrogen: Deuterium (easily extracted from seawater) and Tritium. This means the fuel supply for fusion is virtually inexhaustible and produces no long-lived high-level radioactive waste.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the Kessler Syndrome in the context of outer space activities?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: Gradual cooling of the Sun’s core
options.B: Biological effects of zero gravity on human bone density
options.C: Disruption of satellite communication during solar flares
options.D: A self-sustaining cascade of collisions between objects in Earth’s orbit

questions.explanation:
Kessler Syndrome (also known as collisional cascading) is a theoretical scenario proposed by NASA scientist Donald J. Kessler in 1978. It describes a situation where the density of space junk and objects in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) becomes so high that a single collision creates a massive cloud of shrapnel. This new debris then acts as uncontrollable projectiles, striking other satellites and generating even more debris, creating a dangerous, self-sustaining domino effect.

Additional Facts:

3 Project NETRA: This is an early warning system in space developed by ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) to detect debris and other hazards to Indian satellites. It stands for Network for space object Tracking and Analysis.

3 “Graveyard Orbit”: To prevent the Kessler Syndrome, international space guidelines recommend that when geosynchronous satellites reach the end of their operational life, they should be pushed into a higher “graveyard orbit” safely out of the way of operational traffic.

3 Anti-Satellite (ASAT) Tests: India’s “Mission Shakti” in 2019 successfully tested an ASAT weapon. While highly strategic, such kinetic tests are globally controversial precisely because they generate thousands of pieces of new orbital debris.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs regarding Directed Energy Weapon systems and their countries of origin are correctly matched? 1. HELIOS : United States of America 2. Peresvet : United Kingdom 3. Silent Hunter : China 4. IDD&IS Mk2A : India Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Pair 1 is correctly matched: HELIOS (High Energy Laser with Integrated Optical-dazzler and Surveillance) is a highly advanced laser weapon system developed by Lockheed Martin for the United States. It is primarily integrated into US Navy warships to blind or physically destroy hostile drones and fast-attack boats.

Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Peresvet laser complex is a strategic directed energy weapon developed by Russia, not the UK. It is reportedly designed to blind enemy optical reconnaissance satellites. The United Kingdom’s flagship DEW programs are the DragonFire high-power laser and the Radio Frequency Directed Energy Weapon (RFDEW).

Pair 3 is correctly matched: The Silent Hunter (along with the Hurricane-3000) is a prominent laser air-defence system developed by China. It is explicitly designed to counter the growing threat of low-altitude, slow-moving drone swarms by burning through their fuselage.

45

Pair 4 is correctly matched: The IDD&IS (Integrated Drone Detection and Interdiction System) Mk2A is an indigenous Indian system developed by the DRDO. It is a comprehensive anti-drone umbrella that features “hard kill” (laser-based DEW) capabilities to neutralise aerial threats.

Additional Facts:

3 The Cost-Per-Shot Advantage: The greatest strategic advantage of DEWs is their economics. Traditional surface-to-air missiles can cost millions of dollars each, creating an unsustainable cost-exchange ratio when shooting down a $2,000 commercial drone. A laser weapon, however, costs very less worth of electricity per shot and has a virtually limitless “magazine” as long as the generator has fuel.

3 Limitations of DEWs: Laser weapons currently face significant environmental limitations. Heavy rain, dense fog, dust storms, and atmospheric turbulence can scatter the laser beam, severely reducing its effective range and lethality.

3 KALI Project: Apart from the IDD&IS, India has historically worked on the KALI (Kilo Ampere Linear Injector) project. Jointly developed by the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) and DRDO, it is designed to emit powerful bursts of electromagnetic microwaves to fry the electronic circuitry of incoming missiles.

questions.q: The immunoglobulin abundantly present in colostrum that provides passive immunity to a newborn is:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
The yellowish fluid called colostrum, which is secreted by the mother during the initial days of lactation, has very high concentrations of IgA antibodies. These antibodies protect the infant’s digestive and respiratory tracts from infections during the early, vulnerable stages of life.

IgG: The most abundant antibody in human blood. It is the only antibody capable of crossing the placenta from mother to fetus to provide immunity before birth.

IgE: This antibody is primarily responsible for triggering allergic reactions (like asthma or hay fever) and protecting against parasitic worm infections.

IgM: This is the largest antibody and is always the “first responder” that the body produces when fighting a new infection.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding cruise and ballistic missiles are correct? 1. Ballistic missiles are powered primarily during the initial launch phase, whereas cruise missiles remain continuously powered during flight. 2. Cruise missiles remain within the Earth’s atmosphere, whereas ballistic missiles may follow a trajectory extending into the exoatmosphere. 3. In India’s missile arsenal, the Agni series are cruise missiles, while BrahMos is a ballistic missile. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Statement 1 is correct: Ballistic missiles operate essentially like a thrown rock; they are propelled by heavy rocket engines only during the initial boost phase and then rely on gravity and momentum to fall onto their target. Cruise missiles, however, operate more like pilotless aircraft. They are equipped with jet engines (like turbofans or ramjets) that provide continuous thrust for the entirety of their flight.

Statement 2 is correct: Ballistic missiles follow a distinct, high-arcing parabolic (sub-orbital) trajectory. Long-range ballistic missiles will completely exit the Earth’s atmosphere into space before re-entering to strike. Cruise missiles, on the other hand, fly Aerodynamically. They stay entirely within the atmosphere and often fly extremely close to the ground (terrain-hugging) to avoid enemy radar detection.

Statement 3 is incorrect: The Agni series (Agni I to Agni V) is India’s premier surface-to-surface ballistic missile, capable of carrying nuclear warheads over intercontinental distances. The BrahMos (jointly developed with Russia) is a supersonic Cruise missile, renowned for its extreme speed and precision manoeuvring.

Additional Facts:

3 Because ballistic missiles re-enter the atmosphere at hypersonic speeds (often Mach 15-20 for ICBMs), they are incredibly difficult to shoot down in their terminal phase.

3 Cruise missiles are much slower, but they are difficult to intercept because their low-altitude flight path hides them beneath the “radar horizon” until they are very close to the target.

3 Ballistic missiles are specifically designed to carry heavier payloads, particularly strategic nuclear warheads, over thousands of kilometres. Cruise missiles generally carry smaller, conventional high-explosive payloads for pinpoint surgical strikes (though some can be nuclear-armed).

3 Nirbhay Missile: Aside from BrahMos, India has also indigenously developed the ‘Nirbhay’ missile, which is a long-range, subsonic cruise missile designed by the DRDO.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs of prominent global air defence systems and their primary developing countries/regions: 1. Iron Dome : Israel 2. Patriot : United Kingdom 3. HQ-9 : China 4. SAMP/T(Mamba) : Russia How many pairs of the given above are correctly matched?
questions.question_type: Numerical/Calculation — Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Pair 1 is correctly matched: The Iron Dome is a highly renowned, battle-tested mobile air defence

46

system developed by Rafael Advanced Defence Systems in Israel. It is specifically designed to intercept and destroy short-range rockets and artillery shells fired from close distances.

Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Patriot (Phased Array Tracking Radar to Intercept on Target) system is strictly an American-made surface-to-air missile system. Developed primarily by Raytheon, it is the primary high-altitude defence system used by the United States Army and widely exported to allied nations.

Pair 3 is correctly matched: The HQ-9 is China’s premier domestic medium-to-long-range, active radar homing surface-to-air missile system. It is heavily analogous to the Russian S-300 and the American Patriot systems, providing comprehensive fleet and territorial air defence for the Chinese military.

Pair 4 is incorrectly matched: The SAMP/T (Surface-to-Air Missile Platform/Terrain) is a purely European air defence architecture. It was jointly developed by France and Italy through the Eurosam consortium. It utilises the Aster 30 missile to intercept aircraft and short-range ballistic missiles.

Additional Facts:

3 THAAD (Terminal High Altitude Area Defence): Another critical United States system, THAAD is designed to shoot down short, medium, and intermediate-range ballistic missiles in their terminal phase (descent or reentry) using a hit-to-kill approach.

3 Arrow 3: Co-developed by Israel and the United States, this system handles exoatmospheric interception. It is designed to destroy longrange ballistic missiles while they are still in space, far above the Earth’s atmosphere.

questions.q: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) primarily targets and destroys which of the following cells of the human immune system?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
HIV belongs to a specialised group of viruses called retroviruses, meaning it carries its genetic information in the form of RNA rather than DNA. Once HIV enters the human body (often initially taking shelter in macrophages), it specifically seeks out, infects, and replicates within Helper T-lymphocytes.

As the virus multiplies, it destroys these Helper T-cells in the process. Because Helper T-cells are the “command centres” that stimulate B-cells to make antibodies and activate other immune responses, their drastic depletion leaves the body completely vulnerable. This severe weakening of the immune system is what characterises Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS), making the patient highly susceptible to opportunistic infections (like tuberculosis or pneumonia) that a healthy immune system would normally fend off easily.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of major vectorborne diseases and their primary causative agents or vectors is incorrectly matched?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: Malaria: Caused by a protozoan parasite and transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito.
options.B: Dengue: A viral disease transmitted by the Aedes aegypti mosquito, which primarily bites during the daytime.
options.C: Chikungunya: Caused by a bacterial infection and transmitted primarily by the Aedes mosquito.
options.D: Lymphatic Filariasis: Caused by a parasitic nematode worm and commonly transmitted by the Culex mosquito.

questions.explanation:
Pair 1 is correctly matched: Malaria is not caused by a virus or a bacterium, but by a protozoan parasite of the genus Plasmodium (such as P. falciparum or P. vivax). It is transmitted to humans exclusively through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes, which typically bite between dusk and dawn.

Pair 2 is correctly matched: Dengue is a viral infection caused by the Dengue virus (DENV). It is transmitted primarily by infected female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. Unlike the malaria vector, Aedes mosquitoes are predominantly daybiters and breed in clean, stagnant artificial water containers.

Pair 3 is incorrectly matched: Chikungunya is not a bacterial infection. It is a viral disease caused by the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV). However, the second half of the statement is true; it shares the exact same transmitting vector as Dengue, the Aedes mosquito. The disease is characterised by an abrupt onset of fever, frequently accompanied by severe, debilitating joint pain.

Pair 4 is correctly matched: Lymphatic Filariasis (commonly referred to as Elephantiasis) is caused by infection with parasitic nematode worms, most commonly Wuchereria bancrofti. In India, the primary transmitting vector is the Culex quinquefasciatus mosquito. The parasite severely impairs the lymphatic system, leading to the abnormal and painful enlargement of body parts.

Additional Facts:

3 Acute Encephalitis Syndrome (AES) is locally known as “Chamki Fever” in Bihar. Outbreaks frequently occur in Muzaffarpur, Bihar. While some AES cases are vector-borne (like Japanese Encephalitis, transmitted by Culex mosquitoes), the specific Muzaffarpur outbreaks have been strongly linked to a naturally occurring toxin (MCPG) found in unripe litchi fruits consumed by malnourished children.

47

3 The Government of India has set aggressive public health targets to eliminate these diseases: Lymphatic Filariasis by 2027 and Malaria by 2030.

3 Platelet Drop: A defining clinical characteristic of severe Dengue fever (often called “breakbone fever” due to intense joint pain) is a rapid, dangerous drop in the patient’s blood platelet count (thrombocytopenia).

3 Quinine: The oldest and most famous antimalarial drug, Quinine, is naturally extracted from the bark of the Cinchona tree.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs of astronomical observatories in India and their locations: 1. Udaipur Solar Observatory : Rajasthan 2. Kodaikanal Solar Observatory : Kerala 3. Gauribidanur Radio Observatory : Karnataka 4. Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES) : Himachal Pradesh How many pairs of the given above are correctly matched?
questions.question_type: Numerical/Calculation — Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Pair 1 is correctly matched: The Udaipur Solar Observatory is located on an island in Fateh Sagar Lake in Rajasthan. It is managed by the Physical Research Laboratory. It is considered one of the best solar observing sites in Asia.

Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: The Kodaikanal Solar Observatory is located in the Palani Hills of Tamil Nadu, not Kerala. It is historically significant and is operated by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.

Pair 3 is correctly matched: The Gauribidanur Radio Observatory is located near Bengaluru in Karnataka. It is jointly operated by the Raman Research Institute and the Indian Institute of Astrophysics. It operates a dedicated radio heliograph to monitor the solar corona.

Pair 4 is incorrectly matched: The Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES) is located in Nainital, Uttarakhand, not Himachal Pradesh. It is an autonomous institute that conducts extensive research in solar physics and atmospheric sciences.

Additional Facts:

3 Aditya-L1 Mission: This is India’s first dedicated space-based solar observatory. It was successfully launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) using the PSLV-C57 rocket.

3 Lagrange Point 1: The Aditya-L1 spacecraft is placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange point 1 (L1). This strategic position provides a continuous, uninterrupted view of the Sun without any occultation or eclipses.

3 MAST Telescope: The Multi Application Solar Telescope (MAST) is a prominent facility operationalized at the Udaipur Solar Observatory. It provides highly detailed 3D velocity and magnetic field models of active solar flares.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs regarding vaccine types and their mechanisms of action: 1. mRNA vaccines: Deliver genetic instructions for host cells to produce antigenic proteins 2. Live-attenuated vaccines: Introduce a chemically killed pathogen to stimulate immunity 3. Viral vector vaccines: Use a modified harmless virus to deliver the target genetic material 4. Toxoid vaccines: Use isolated surface proteins or polysaccharides of the pathogen Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
3 Pair 1 is correctly matched: mRNA vaccines (like the Pfizer or Moderna COVID-19 vaccines) use a tiny piece of messenger RNA wrapped in a protective lipid nanoparticle to enter host cells. Once inside, they instruct the cells to temporarily build a specific viral protein (like the spike protein), which strongly stimulates both B-cells (humoral immunity) and T-cells (cellular immunity).

3 Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: Live-attenuated vaccines (like MMR or BCG) use a living, but severely weakened form of the pathogen that closely mimics a natural infection to create a very strong and long-lasting cellular immune response. The mechanism described in the pair, using a chemically killed pathogen, actually describes an Inactivated vaccine (like Covaxin or the Salk polio vaccine).

3 Pair 3 is correctly matched: Viral vector vaccines (like Covishield/AstraZeneca or Sputnik V) take a completely different, harmless virus (often an adenovirus) and modify it to act as a Trojan horse. This “vector” delivers the genetic code of the target pathogen into our cells to trigger a robust cellular and humoral immune response.

3 Pair 4 is incorrectly matched: Toxoid vaccines (like those for Tetanus or Diphtheria) use an inactivated version of the harmful toxin produced by the bacteria, rather than targeting the bacteria itself. The mechanism described in the pair, using an isolated protein or sugar capsule, actually describes a Subunit or Conjugate vaccine (like the Hepatitis B vaccine).

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the fundamental operational infrastructure of satellite broadband internet systems?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: Geostationary satellites transmit data directly between user terminals, requiring no ground stations.
options.B: An orbiting satellite constellation links with terrestrial gateway stations to wirelessly transmit internet data.
options.C: Satellites relay internet signals by bouncing transmissions off the ionosphere toward ground receivers.
options.D: LEO satellites communicate solely via intersatellite laser links, completely bypassing all ground-based infrastructure.

questions.explanation:
Option A is incorrect: While satellites do transmit data, they do not operate completely independently of the ground. They absolutely require terrestrial gateway stations to interface with the global fibreoptic internet backbone. They cannot just exclusively bounce signals between individual user terminals.

Option B is correct: Satellite broadband provides direct wireless internet connectivity. It uses communication satellites actively orbiting the Earth. The physical infrastructure fundamentally

48

requires a space segment composed of satellite constellations. It also strictly necessitates a ground segment featuring gateway stations and network control centres to connect to the wider global internet.

Option C is incorrect: Bouncing radio waves off the ionosphere is a standard propagation technique for long-distance amateur (ham) radio. This specific atmospheric method is physically incapable of supporting the high-bandwidth frequencies required for broadband internet.

Option D is incorrect: Modern Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites do utilise inter-satellite laser links. This reduces global routing latency by passing data across the constellation. However, they cannot completely bypass ground-based infrastructure. The data must eventually be beamed down to a terrestrial gateway to reach standard terrestrial servers.

Additional Facts:

3 Latency: Satellite internet typically suffers from higher latency compared to terrestrial wired connections. This delay occurs because data must physically travel thousands of kilometres up to the space segment and back down to the user.

3 LEO Megaconstellations: Modern projects rely heavily on Low Earth Orbit (LEO) under 2,000 km altitude. This drastically reduces the signal latency that historically plagued older Geostationary (GEO) internet satellites.

3 The socio-economic objective of these systems is universal connectivity. They are uniquely capable of providing reliable, high-speed broadband to difficult mountainous or rural terrains where laying underground optical fibre is economically unviable.

3 Key Global Projects: Prominent operational and planned megaconstellations include SpaceX’s Starlink, Amazon’s Project Kuiper, Eutelsat’s OneWeb, and China’s Qianfan constellation.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a Sunsynchronous polar orbit?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: An orbit that remains fixed over a single point above the Earth’s equator
options.B: A near-polar orbit in which the satellite passes over a given location at nearly the same local solar time
options.C: A highly elliptical orbit designed for prolonged coverage of high-latitude regions
options.D: A low-Earth orbit that moves west to east to utilise Earth’s rotational velocity

questions.explanation:
Sun-Synchronous Orbit (SSO) is a specific type of near-polar orbit. The satellite’s orbital plane rotates (precesses) at the same rate at which the Earth revolves around the Sun. Consequently, the satellite maintains a constant relationship with the Sun, ensuring it passes over any specific location on the Earth’s surface at the same local solar time every day. This provides consistent lighting conditions, which are essential for Earth-observation and imaging missions like NISAR.

Geostationary Orbit (GEO): While ISRO’s GSLV rocket is typically used for placement in Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO) to reach GEO, NISAR marks the first time a GSLV was used to place a satellite into a Sun-Synchronous Orbit.

Molniya orbits are highly inclined, highly elliptical orbits designed to provide consistent satellite coverage over polar and high-latitude regions where geostationary satellites are less effective.

Prograde Orbit: While many launches use the Earth’s rotation for a “boost,” Sun-Synchronous orbits are often “retrograde” (slightly opposite to Earth’s rotation) to achieve the specific nodal precession required to stay in sync with the Sun.

Additional Facts:

3 NISAR was launched in July 2025 using ISRO’s GSLV-F16 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

3 Dual-Band Innovation: It is the world’s first Earth observation satellite to integrate both L-band (provided by NASA) and S-band (provided by ISRO) Synthetic Aperture Radar on a single platform.

3 Large-Scale Deployment: Following the launch, the mission successfully deployed a massive 12-metre diameter common unfurlable reflector antenna.

3 Advanced Imaging: It utilises SweepSAR technology to produce high-resolution, wideswath images. The radar works by sending out energy pulses and recording the reflection back from Earth’s surface.

3 Monitoring Capability: With a mission life of 5 years, it provides high-resolution data every 12 days (repeat cycle) to monitor land and ice changes across the globe.

3 Global Collaboration: The mission follows an Open-Data Policy, making its findings freely available to the global scientific community.

questions.q: Which of the following bacterial pathogens is specifically responsible for causing the disease Splenic fever?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Anthrax is a severe, often fatal, infectious disease caused by the rod-shaped, Gram-positive bacterium Bacillus anthracis. It primarily affects herbivorous livestock (like sheep and cattle) but can be transmitted to humans through contact with infected animals or their products, causing severe respiratory, gastrointestinal, or skin infections.

49

Bacillus cereus: Primarily causes foodborne illnesses (food poisoning), famously associated with reheated fried rice.

Yersinia pestis: The causative agent of the Plague (Bubonic, Septicemic, and Pneumonic), historically known as the Black Death.

Clostridium perfringens: A common cause of severe food poisoning and the primary agent responsible for gas gangrene in wounds.

Mycobacterium tuberculosis: The causative agent of Tuberculosis (TB).

Clostridium tetani: The causative agent of Tetanus (Lockjaw).

Vibrio cholerae: The causative agent of Cholera.

Additional facts:

3 Dietary Fibre: Often considered a “nonnutrient” carbohydrate, it is a polysaccharide (cellulose) that humans cannot digest but is essential for gut health.

3 Major vs. Trace Minerals: Minerals like Calcium and Magnesium are “Major Minerals” (needed in >100mg/day), whereas Iron and Iodine are “Trace Minerals.”

3 Fat-Soluble Vitamins: Unlike the watersoluble examples above, Vitamins A, D, E, and K require dietary fat for absorption and can be stored in the liver.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains the significance of a lower nanometer (nm) rating in modern mobile processors?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: It indicates a smaller transistor size, enabling more transistors per chip, higher processing speed and lower power consumption
options.B: It measures the clock frequency of the processor in nanoseconds, directly determining how many instructions are executed per second
options.C: It specifies the thickness of the thermal paste layer applied between the processor die and the heat sink during manufacturing
options.D: It denotes the physical length of the copper interconnect pathways connecting the processor to RAM modules on the motherboard

questions.explanation:
The nanometer (nm) rating historically refers to the physical dimensions of individual transistors on a semiconductor chip. A lower nm rating signifies that the transistors are physically smaller. This allows manufacturers to pack billions more transistors onto a single silicon die. Smaller transistors require lower electrical voltage to switch states. The reduced physical distance also means electrons travel faster between components. This directly results in higher processing speeds and significantly enhanced battery efficiency.

Additional Facts:

3 Moore’s Law: An empirical observation formulating that the number of transistors on a microchip doubles approximately every two years. This economic and technological driver pushes the industry toward increasingly smaller nodes (e.g., 5nm, 3nm).

3 Quantum Tunnelling: As transistors shrink toward the 2nm threshold, the insulating barriers become perilously thin. Electrons can spontaneously “tunnel” through these barriers. This causes severe electrical leakage and heat generation.

3 Transistor Architecture: To combat quantum leakage, the industry shifted from flat planar transistors to complex 3D structures. These include Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFET) and Gate-All-Around (GAA) architectures. They wrap the gate around the electron channel to prevent leakage.

3 India Semiconductor Mission (ISM): A flagship initiative launched by the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY). It operates with a massive ₹76,000 crore outlay. It aims to establish a robust, indigenous semiconductor manufacturing and design ecosystem to ensure technological sovereignty.

questions.q: Which of the following pathogens is a causative agent for pneumonia in humans?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation:
Haemophilus influenzae is the bacterial causative agent of pneumonia, along with Streptococcus pneumoniae. The infection inflames the alveoli, filling them with fluid and impairing gaseous exchange.

Salmonella typhi causes Typhoid fever, a systemic infection primarily affecting the gastrointestinal tract.

Mycobacterium leprae causes Leprosy (Hansen’s disease), a chronic disease affecting the skin and peripheral nerves.
